page: Amazon Web Services i8g.16xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and 64-bit ARM architecture. It features 64 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz, with one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, alongside a bundled 15,000 GB local NVMe SSD storage array. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 38 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25% and top 10% respectively. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, scoring in the top 10% across both small-block cached and large-block uncached read and write tests. The instance also demonstrates top-tier performance in Passmark database operations, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and static web serving throughput. However, single-core CPU benchmarks, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, perform in the average middle 50% range.

While the server excels in multi-threaded tasks and memory-intensive operations, it exhibits a tradeoff in specific workloads, such as text generation for small LLM models, which falls into the bottom 25%. Conversely, text generation for medium and large LLM models ranks in the top 10% and top 25% respectively. Given the massive local NVMe storage capacity, high memory bandwidth, and strong database operation benchmarks, this instance is designed for large-scale databases, data warehousing, and high-throughput web serving.

Single-core performance remains in the average middle 50% tier. The server exhibits high resource density, making it highly cost-efficient for storage-heavy and memory-intensive workloads. It is optimized for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, and multi-threaded data processing, though it shows lower efficiency in small-model LLM text generation.
